subject: Re: IP indemnity evidence request and liability carve-out — action plan
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@datasight.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, procurement@datasight.com
Cc: Mark Johnson <mark.johnson@datasight.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: carve-out to liability cap for IP/infringement indemnity

Evelyn — thanks for the conversation last week. As we prepare to finalize the Order Form and MSA redlines, DataSight Legal has flagged one open point we need agreed language on: the liability cap and whether IP indemnity (patent/copyright/trademark infringement) should be carved out from the monetary cap.

High level ask: carve out direct damages arising from third-party IP claims that Redwood indemnifies for from the overall liability cap (or, alternatively, provide express indemnity with an evidence/resolution process that can resolve claims without exposure to the full cap).

We also need a reasonably scoped evidence package from Redwood to feel comfortable — list of relevant patents/third-party notices procedures, any available patent opinions (if you have them), and an indemnity playbook that explains remediation/defense steps.

Attached: DataSight redline of the MSA (see docx) — we’ve highlighted the proposed carve-out.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to: 1) accept a limited carve-out for indemnified IP claims (we’re open to “as a result of a third-party claim” language), or 2) provide operational mitigations (escrow/defensive termination rights, bind indemnity counsel, expedited remediation) that will make us comfortable keeping IP liability inside the cap?

We need to finish contract terms by end of next week to hit our internal procurement target. Happy to set a 30-minute legal-to-legal call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
Sr. Counsel — Commercial
DataSight Analytics

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: carve-out to liability cap for IP/infringement indemnity — draft language

Evelyn — draft language below. I’m trying to keep it narrowly tailored so we don’t open floodgates. Two tracks: (1) carve-out language DataSight can accept now; (2) operational alternative if we can’t agree to an uncapped exposure.

Option A — Limited carve-out (clean):
"Notwithstanding the limitations on liability set forth herein, Redwood shall not be subject to the liability cap with respect to amounts payable under its indemnification obligations for third‑party claims alleging that Redwood’s services infringe a United States or European patent, copyright, or trademark, provided that such claim arises from (i) the use of the Service as provided under this Agreement and (ii) a final adjudication or settlement for which Redwood is obligated to pay. Redwood’s indemnity obligations under this Section shall be subject to the other limitations and procedures set forth in this Agreement (including prompt notice and cooperation)."

Option B — Operationally bounded alternative: (keeps cap but provides resolution path)
"Redwood’s liability for indemnified IP claims shall be subject to the liability cap in Section X; provided, however, that the parties agree to an expedited resolution process: Redwood will (i) promptly investigate, (ii) retain counsel to defend at Redwood’s expense if necessary, (iii) provide a remediation plan within 30 days, and (iv) offer, at its option, replacement functionality, a license, or reimbursement limited to amounts reasonably necessary to secure continued use. For claims that survive remediation and result in a final adjudication, the parties’ damages shall be limited to direct damages reasonably incurred in connection with such adjudication and not to exceed the amount set forth in Section X for indemnified claims."

Comments: Option A is clean but increases potential exposure. We can narrow further to require final adjudication (i.e., Redwood pays only if found liable in a court or binding arbitration) or to carve out only for IP claims arising from Redwood-developed model components (exclude customer-provided code/data).

I’ve attached a tracked redline with both options called out (Redlines_MSA_Datasight_v2.docx). Rishi — I marked the places where we need evidence/artifact support (patent ledger, model provenance).

Marissa
Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: carve-out to liability cap for IP/infringement indemnity — evidence and ops notes

Couple operational points to add to the packet — these will help convince procurement without giving full uncapped liability:
- Evidence pack (attached): Patent-Ledger-Summary.pdf (high-level list of patents owned by Redwood or third-party licenses we rely on), Evidence-Checklist.xlsx (shows what we can produce within 5 business days).
- Defensive steps we can commit to: (1) bind counsel selection for indemnity claims (we’ll agree to use our counsel but allow DataSight to consent not to be unreasonably withheld), (2) mediation within 45 days before escalation to litigation, (3) ability to offer replacement functionality or license where practicable, (4) escrow of model checkpoints only under strict terms (cost/ops constraints noted).
- Carve-out scope suggestion: carve out Redwood’s payments for third-party adjudicated infringement claims but exclude hypothetical consequential damages (lost profits, punitive) and exclude claims arising out of Customer’s modifications or inputs.

Draft short paragraph to attach to the MSA redline (for consideration):
"For the avoidance of doubt, amounts paid by Redwood to resolve a third‑party claim of infringement that is the subject of Redwood’s indemnity shall be excluded from the liability cap, provided that such amounts are for direct damages and remediation costs resulting from final adjudication or settlement and do not include consequential or punitive damages, and further provided that such claim does not arise from Customer’s materials or modifications."

I think if we present Option A with the above clarifications, and the evidence pack, DataSight will accept without exec escalation.

Rishi
Head of Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

1) Redwood will accept a carve-out from the liability cap for indemnified third‑party IP claims limited to direct remediation/settlement amounts following final adjudication or binding settlement; consequential damages remain excluded.
2) Redwood will provide the evidence pack as proposed (patent ledger + checklist) within 3 business days of execution.
3) The MSA will include the operational commitments Rishi outlined (bind counsel process, 30-day remediation plan, mediation step).

We’ve updated the attached Order Form & MSA redline to reflect this language — see DocuSign review link below. If you can confirm Redwood’s acceptance of the exact draft language in the DocuSign packet, we’ll route for procurement signature.
